'''Michael Römer''' (born 23 December 1946 in [[Alheim]], [[Hesse]]) is a German business executive, and former chairman and CEO of [[Merck KGaA|Merck]].

He grew up in [[Offenbach am Main]], where his father was an engineer at [[Hoechst AG]] (now [[Sanofi]]). He studied chemistry at the [[Technical University of Darmstadt]] from 1968, and obtained a doctorate in chemistry in 1977. He was employed by Merck from 1978. He became a deputy member of the executive board in 1993 and a regular member in 1994. He became deputy chairman in 2000, and was chairman and CEO from 2005 to 2007.<ref>D. Sulzmann: [http://www.lifepr.de/pressemeldungen/merck-kgaa/boxid-43648.html ''Dr. Michael Römer erhält Verdienstkreuz 1. Klasse.''] In ''lifepr.de'', 19 May 2008.</ref><ref>[http://www.chemie.de/news/d/62076/ ''Merck KGaA: Karl-Ludwig Kley folgt Michael Römer als Vorsitzender der Geschäftsleitung.''] In: ''chemie.de'', 23 February 2007.</ref><ref>[http://www.tagesspiegel.de/wirtschaft/merck-chef-michael-roemer/693106.html ''Merck-Chef Michael Römer.''] In: ''Der Tagesspiegel'', 14 March 2006</ref>

Römer was president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Darmstadt 2000–2009. He received the Officer's Cross of the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]] in 2008.<ref name="wiwo">{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130212212027/http://www.wiwo.de/unternehmen-maerkte/koepfe-der-wirtschaft/michael-roemer-11/biografie/%23herkunft-und-familie|title=''Köpfe der Wirtschaft: Michael Römer.''}} In: ''Wirtschaftswoche.de''.</ref>
